phases.name: Base
phases.description: Build aerobic endurance with steady zone2 riding and gradually longer weekend rides
phases.focus: Time in saddle and aerobic efficiency
phases.coachNote: All rides in zone2 HR or 60-70% FTP. Focus on smooth pedaling and staying comfortable in the saddle for longer durations.

phases.name: Build
phases.description: Introduce threshold and VO2max intervals, extend long ride distance
phases.focus: Threshold power, aerobic capacity, and long-ride fueling
phases.coachNote: Threshold intervals at 95% FTP should feel hard but sustainable. VO2max intervals are very hard — give full effort. Practice nutrition on long rides.

phases.name: Peak
phases.description: Longest rides and century race-pace simulation
phases.focus: Endurance at century distance, race-pace comfort, and fueling strategy
phases.coachNote: These are your longest training rides. Practice your full race-day nutrition plan: eat and drink on schedule, not by feel.

phases.name: Taper
phases.description: Reduce volume, maintain intensity, arrive fresh
phases.coachNote: Volume drops significantly. Keep one short intensity session to stay sharp. Check your bike, pack your kit, plan your aid stations.

Tue.name: Endurance Ride
Tue.description: Steady zone2 ride on flat to rolling terrain
Tue.coachNote: Keep cadence high (85-95 rpm). Focus on smooth, circular pedal strokes.

Thu.name: Endurance Ride
Thu.description: Steady endurance ride with 5min at higher cadence (100+ rpm) in the middle
Thu.coachNote: Cadence drills improve neuromuscular efficiency. Spin easy — no mashing.

Sat.name: Long Endurance Ride
Sat.description: Long steady ride at endurance pace. Bring 1 bottle of water and a snack.
Sat.coachNote: Start easy. The goal is time in saddle, not speed. Find a comfortable pace and enjoy the ride.

Tue.name: VO2max Intervals
Tue.description: Warmup 15min easy + 4×5min @110% FTP (5min easy spin recovery) + Cooldown 10min easy
Tue.coachNote: Early build: 4×4min. Late build: 5×5min. Full effort on each interval — these build top-end power.

Thu.name: Threshold Intervals
Thu.description: Warmup 15min easy + 2×20min @95% FTP (5min easy spin recovery) + Cooldown 10min easy
Thu.coachNote: Smooth, steady power output. Cadence 85-95 rpm. These build your sustainable power for long climbs.

Sat.name: Long Endurance Ride
Sat.description: Long zone2 ride. Bring 2 bottles and 2 snacks. Practice eating and drinking on the bike.
Sat.coachNote: Fuel every 45min: eat before you're hungry, drink before you're thirsty. This is when you learn what your stomach tolerates.

Tue.name: VO2max Intervals
Tue.description: Warmup 15min easy + 5×5min @110% FTP (5min easy spin recovery) + Cooldown 10min easy
Tue.coachNote: Maximum effort intervals. Quality over quantity — if you fade, reduce the number, not the intensity.

Thu.name: Threshold Ride
Thu.description: Warmup 15min easy + 2×20min @95% FTP (5min easy recovery) + Cooldown 10min easy
Thu.coachNote: Maintain threshold power. Consistency across both 20min blocks is the goal.

Sat.name: Long Century Simulation
Sat.description: Longest ride of the plan. Bring 3 bottles and real food. Simulate race-day pacing and fueling.
Sat.coachNote: This is your dress rehearsal. Start easy, pace conservatively. Practice aid station stops: quick, efficient, get back on the bike. Nothing new on race day — test everything now.

Tue.name: Short Threshold
Tue.description: Week 11: Warmup 15min + 15min @95% FTP + Cooldown 15min. Week 12: Easy spin 40min.
Tue.coachNote: Short and sharp. Keep the legs primed without accumulating fatigue. Week 12: just an easy spin.

Thu.name: Easy Spin
Thu.description: Very light recovery spin. High cadence, low resistance.
Thu.coachNote: Active recovery only. No effort — just get the blood flowing. Check your bike is race-ready.

Sat.name: Long Ride (Taper) or Century
Sat.description: Week 11: easy long ride 80km. Week 12: CENTURY RIDE — 160km.
Sat.coachNote: Week 11: one last moderate long ride. Week 12: RACE DAY. Pace yourself — the first 80km should feel easy. Eat and drink on schedule. You've done the training.

overrides.value: CENTURY RIDE — 160km. Your goal. Pace conservatively, fuel consistently, enjoy the achievement.

trainingPlan.name: 12-Week Century Ride
trainingPlan.description: A 12-week plan for cyclists who can comfortably ride 50-80km and want to complete a century ride (160km). Builds from 60km to 150km long rides with threshold, VO2max intervals, and race-day fueling practice.
trainingPlan.goal: Complete a century ride (160km / 100 miles) strong and well-fueled
